newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's CPP rate rises in November vs October.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's CPP rate rises in November vs October.

text.p: Mexico's CPP rose 299 basis points in November from October to 28.03 percent, the Banco de Mexico said Monday.
The CPP, the average bank cost of borrowing from the public, was at 25.04 percent in October.
Banco de Mexico said that the CCP, the average bank term deposit cost measured in pesos in Mexican banks, was 29.01 percent in November compared to 25.79 percent in October.
The CCP will eventually substitute the CPP, with the aim of better reflecting the cost of those term deposits for the banks, the central bank has said.
The Banco de Mexico also said that the CCP-UDIs, the CPP measured in UDIs, an inflation indexed investment unit, was at 7.71 percent in November, down from 7.91 percent in October.
The Banco de Mexico publishes various rates in order to give a better idea to the public of the cost of borrowing.
